key_insight: A learned patient world model can support multiple ICU simulations by changing scenario mappings rather than rebuilding clinical state models.
engineering_relevance: The approach connects history-aware patient predictions to shared calendars, resources, and queues for evaluating ICU capacity and care-dispatch policies.
method: Train a neural patient world model on longitudinal MIMIC-IV EHRs.
Freeze the model and map time-queryable predictions to admissions, care tasks, and discharge proposals.
Simulate ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity scenarios.
evidence_signal: The model matched Markov and semi-Markov comparators on aggregate occupancy and directional policy responses, while capturing a history-dependent 24-hour recovery difference of −6.4 percentage points versus −6.7 observed.
watch_item: Validation beyond MIMIC-IV and careful calibration of scenario-specific mappings remain important before operational deployment.
paper_title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
